title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Nanosonics Staff
tiers.description: Each director, officer and employee of the Nanosonics Group, plus contractors and consultants whose terms of engagement apply this policy to them. Subject to insider trading law, Blackout Periods, the short-term dealing and short-selling rules, and the Board-approval requirements for derivatives and margin/stock loan arrangements.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Each director, each Company Secretary, each member of the Executive Management Team and their direct reports, and any staff member nominated by the Board or Company Secretary. Must give prior notification and obtain clearance from a Notification Officer before any Dealing.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Subset of Designated Persons distinguished for their Notification Officer (Chairman of the Board) and for a standalone post-trade disclosure duty to the Company Secretary within two days of any Dealing.

tiers.name: Close Associates
tiers.description: Family members who may influence or be influenced by a Designated Person, and companies, trusts or other entities controlled by a Designated Person (alone or jointly with other Close Associates).

windows.end_anchor: start of the trading day following the day of release of Half Year Results
start of the trading day following the day of release of Full Year Results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify additional Blackout Periods from time to time. The policy does not state whether such additional periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: Board approval (not merely Notification Officer clearance) is required before dealing in any derivative or other financial product issued by a third party over Nanosonics Securities. A narrow exception may apply where the Securities are a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
rules.evidence: Nanosonics Staff are not permitted to Deal in any Derivatives or other financial products issued over the Securities by third parties, such as banks and other institutions, without the prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: No standalone hedging clause or hedging definition exists, and no distinction is drawn for unvested equity incentive securities. A hedge is caught as a Dealing because it is 'the entry into a Derivative in relation to the Securities', triggering the same Board-approval requirement as section 4.4.
rules.evidence: Includes, in relation to Securities, ... the entry into a Derivative in relation to the Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is caught as a Dealing (agreement to dispose, or a Derivative), requiring Board approval under 4.4; if it involves granting security over the shares it is instead, or additionally, a 'similar funding arrangement' under 4.5.
rules.evidence: or the entry into any agreement to do any of the above things.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short-selling, expressed as borrowing Securities in expectation of a price fall; the express ban is limited to Designated Persons. Other Nanosonics Staff remain subject only to the general short-term dealing restriction.
rules.evidence: Short-selling by Designated Persons (i.e. borrowing Securities in the expectation that the price of the Company's Securities will fall) is also prohibited.

rules.detail: Securities lending is expressly included within the Dealing definition, so it carries the same regime as any other Dealing: Designated Persons must obtain prior notification/approval; other Staff must comply with Blackout Periods and insider trading law but face no separate clearance step.
rules.evidence: This includes, without limitation, engaging in securities lending.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. 'Derivatives' is defined by reference to the Corporations Act s761D definition (which captures CFDs) plus a non-exhaustive list; a CFD over Nanosonics shares is therefore a Derivative issued by a third party requiring Board approval under 4.4.
rules.evidence: Has the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars.

rules.detail: Margin loans (or stock loans, or similar funding arrangements) secured by Nanosonics Securities require prior Board approval, with disclosure to the Company Secretary of key terms including number of Securities, trigger points and the lender's right to sell unilaterally. Not an outright ban.
rules.evidence: Nanosonics Staff must not enter into a margin loan or stock loan arrangement, or similar funding arrangement, without prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: Granting security or any encumbrance over Securities is expressly part of the Dealing definition. In practice an encumbrance connected to financing falls under the 4.5 margin/stock loan/'similar funding arrangement' Board-approval regime; an encumbrance unconnected to financing remains a Dealing subject to Blackout Periods and, for Designated Persons, notification.
rules.evidence: the use of the Securities as security or the grant of any encumbrance over the Securities

rules.detail: 'Similar funding arrangement' is broader than margin or stock loans and would capture a bank loan secured on shares as part of a collar. Requires prior Board approval and disclosure of key terms to the Company Secretary; the Company may in turn have to disclose the arrangement to the market if material.
rules.evidence: Nanosonics Staff must not enter into a margin loan or stock loan arrangement, or similar funding arrangement, without prior approval of the Board.

rules.detail: General discouragement of short-term Dealing, illustrated (not fixed) at around 3 months, plus a catch-all for 'other short-term Dealings'. Subject to the Excluded Dealings carve-outs in 4.6.
rules.evidence: Nanosonics Staff may not Deal in Nanosonics' Securities for short-term gain. Short-term Dealing includes buying and selling Securities within a short period (e.g. 3 months) and includes entering into other short-term Dealings.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (disclosure of key terms of any margin/stock loan or similar funding arrangement)
clearance.evidence: Nanosonics Staff are not permitted to Deal in any Derivatives or other financial products issued over the Securities by third parties ... without the prior approval of the Board.

clearance.approver: Chairman (applications by a director or Managing Director); Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee (application by the Chairman); Managing Director (application by the Company Secretary); Company Secretary (all other cases)
clearance.evidence: In exceptional circumstances Nanosonics Staff may be given prior written clearance to dispose of (but not acquire) Nanosonics Securities where they would otherwise be restricted due to the operation of a Blackout Period.

clearance.approver: Notification Officer per Schedule 2 (varies by role)
clearance.evidence: A Designated Person may only Deal in the Securities if they first: (a) complete and forward a Notification to Deal in the Securities ... and (b) receive confirmation ... signed by the Notification Officer, to allow them to Deal in the Securities.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable, no more than two days after any Dealing
clearance.evidence: Directors must notify the Company Secretary as soon as practicable after any Dealing in Nanosonics Securities occurs and, in any case no more than two days after any Dealing.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Trigger points must be disclosed to the Company Secretary as part of seeking Board approval for a margin/stock loan or similar funding arrangement, but the policy gives no independent price-trigger guidance of its own.
financing_disclosure: Nanosonics Staff (all); trigger: prior to entering a margin loan, stock loan or similar funding arrangement (inception); disclose number of Securities, trigger points and the lender's right to sell unilaterally to the Company Secretary as part of seeking Board approval; deadline: before entering the arrangement.
Company; trigger: where required by law or good practice having regard to materiality; discloses margin/stock lending arrangements to the market; deadline: not specified.

exemption_authority: Board approval required for derivatives (4.4) and for margin/stock loan or similar funding arrangements (4.5). Chairman, Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, Managing Director or Company Secretary (depending on the applicant) may grant hardship clearance to dispose of (not acquire) securities during a Blackout Period (4.3.2).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Nanosonics Staff are not permitted to Deal in any Derivatives or other financial products issued over the Securities by third parties, such as banks and other institutions, without the prior approval of the Board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put and call written with a bank falls squarely within this clause; the collar's derivative legs need Board approval, not merely Notification Officer clearance, for every tier and any vesting state.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An exception may apply where the Securities form a component of a listed portfolio or index product.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This narrow carve-out would not cover a bespoke bilateral OTC collar written specifically over Nanosonics shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Nanosonics Staff must not enter into a margin loan or stock loan arrangement, or similar funding arrangement, without prior approval of the Board. In order to obtain such approval, they must disclose the key terms of any such arrangement to the Company Secretary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies with an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar is permitted subject to Board pre-approval and disclosure of trigger points and the lender's unilateral sale rights.

bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of Nanosonics Securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under an approved arrangement (Excluded Dealing)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Provided the financing was Board-approved beforehand, the bank's enforcement sale on a default or knock-out is excluded from the Blackout Period ban rather than being a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company will disclose margin lending or stock lending arrangements to the market where required by law or good practice, having regard to the materiality of the arrangements to the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A sizeable collar loan secured on an executive's shareholding may trigger public ASX disclosure of the arrangement's existence and terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: unless, in the meantime, the Designated Person becomes in possession of Inside Information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar for a Designated Person must be executed within the 5-business-day validity window and becomes unexecutable if inside information arises before signing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: insider trading exemption for plan securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: the insider trading provisions do not apply to applications for, and acquisitions under those applications of, Nanosonics Securities by Nanosonics Staff under any Nanosonics employee equity plan ... Notwithstanding this exemption ... Designated Persons must still give notice and seek approval of proposed acquisitions of Nanosonics Securities under an employee equity plan pursuant to section 5.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where the statutory insider-trading bar does not apply to acquiring vested plan securities, internal notification/approval is still required, affecting timing of a collar entered around vesting or exercise.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy extends to the Close Associates of a Designated Person in relation to Nanosonics Securities ... Designated Persons must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Close Associates comply with this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, dependant or controlled entity does not avoid the Board-approval and notification requirements.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy but is gated by internal approvals rather than banned. The derivative legs require prior Board approval under section 4.4 (any third-party derivative over Nanosonics Securities), and the loan leg, being a 'similar funding arrangement' secured by shares, requires prior Board approval and disclosure to the Company Secretary of the number of securities, trigger points and the lender's right to sell unilaterally under section 4.5. Designated Persons additionally need Notification Officer clearance (valid 5 business days) before dealing, and Directors must confirm price and quantity to the Company Secretary within two days of dealing. Execution, unwind or a lender's forced sale must generally sit outside the 21-day pre-results Blackout Periods, though a forced sale under a Board-approved arrangement is an Excluded Dealing rather than a breach. Because 'similar funding arrangement' and third-party derivatives are approved rather than prohibited, and the forced-sale carve-out exists, this policy is comparatively more accommodating of a funded collar than policies with an outright secured-financing ban, provided Board approval, disclosure and blackout timing are all managed.
